setup.title: From a Pencil Sketch to a Frame of Game (v2): One Maker Builds an NVIDIA GPU
setup.style: Live-action, cinematic, realistic product-documentary look: macro inserts of materials and machines, warm practical lighting at home, cool industrial lighting in the fab.

cast.name: Daniel
cast.description: Daniel, a man in his early thirties with short dark-brown hair, a short neat beard and black rectangular glasses, wearing a charcoal-grey crew-neck sweater over a white T-shirt, dark jeans and grey sneakers.

extras.voice: Daniel, speaking in voice-over, a man in his early thirties with a calm, warm baritone voice, an unhurried pace and a neutral American accent (S1),
extras.music: Minimal electronic ambient score with a soft pulsing synth arpeggio and light percussion, kept at low volume beneath the narration throughout.
extras.speech: Daniel narrates his own build in first-person voice-over, like a maker documentary; he is rarely seen speaking on camera.
extras.framing: This is a making-of film about the GPU, not a portrait. Most shots are object-focused inserts where only the maker's hands and sleeves are visible; when the maker himself is shown, use medium or wide framing and never a facial close-up.

shots.prompt:
The shot opens inside a compact home studio late at night, enveloped in deep shadows except for a solitary pool of warm amber light. An angled desk lamp illuminates the rich grain of a dark wooden worktable, casting soft reflections and elongated shadows across the quiet room. The surrounding space remains muted in deep twilight blues and blacks, creating an intimate, focused atmosphere that emphasizes the solitary nature of an overnight project.

Daniel, a man in his early thirties with short dark-brown hair, a neat beard, and black rectangular glasses, appears as a small figure within the wide room. Dressed in a charcoal-grey crew-neck sweater over a white T-shirt with dark jeans and grey sneakers, he pulls back a chair and sits down at the desk. He places a dark ceramic coffee mug near the lamp's base, then draws a hardbound grid notebook toward himself and smoothly flips it open to a blank spread. Speaking in a calm voice-over about designing an NVIDIA GPU from scratch tonight, he rests his hands beside the pristine paper, prepared to work.

The camera captures the scene from an eye-level wide establishing shot, executing a steady, subtle push-in toward the illuminated desk. Throughout the gentle forward move, the environment and furniture dominate the composition, keeping Daniel in modest proportion without approaching a facial close-up. The warm desk lamp, the steaming mug, and the crisp, untouched grid pages remain clearly visible as the camera drifts closer.

annotation.beat: Night in a small home studio lit by one warm desk lamp. Daniel, small in the frame, sits down at a wooden desk with a coffee mug and opens a blank grid notebook. In voice-over he says tonight he will design his own NVIDIA GPU from scratch.

state.gpu_stage: blank notebook page

shots.prompt:
The shot looks directly down onto the warm wooden desk in the quiet home studio, illuminated by the focused golden glow of a nearby desk lamp. The soft, directional beam casts gentle diagonal shadows across the honey-toned wood grain and highlights the pale grid paper of an open hardcover notebook. The mood is calm, studious, and intimate, isolated from the dark room outside the light's pool.

The notebook lies open flat, its gridded pages initially pristine and blank. Daniel’s right hand enters the frame, framed by the textured cuff of his charcoal-grey crew-neck sweater. Holding a sharpened graphite drafting pencil with steady fingers, he begins mapping out a silicon architecture. His hand sketches a broad, segmented rectangle across the grid lines, dividing the core layout. He draws a central horizontal band representing the shared L2 cache, then methodically outlines rows of identical small squares flanking it on both sides for the streaming multiprocessor blocks. Finally, he adds small rectangular nodes along the outer perimeter to indicate memory controllers. Fine graphite deposits glint lightly under the warm bulb, leaving a clear, hand-drawn GPU block diagram fully established across the page by the end of the shot.

The camera maintains a strict top-down close-up framing, centered directly over the notebook as the diagram takes shape. The shot remains locked off with a subtle, barely perceptible macro drift inward. Only Daniel’s hand, his woollen grey sleeve, the pencil, and the crisp graphite strokes remain visible, keeping the technical sketch at the absolute center of attention.

annotation.beat: Top-down on the notebook: Daniel's hand in a grey sweater sleeve sketches the GPU architecture in pencil, a grid of identical streaming-multiprocessor blocks with an L2 cache bar through the middle and memory controllers on the edges.

state.gpu_stage: pencil block diagram of a GPU on paper

shots.prompt:
The shot opens in an intimate macro view over Daniel's home studio desk, centered entirely on the textured surface of the sketchpad. Warm golden light from an articulated desk lamp rakes across the cream-coloured paper from a low angle, casting microscopic shadows into the tooth of the paper and illuminating stray flecks of rubber eraser crumbs scattered across the margins. The atmosphere is quiet, contemplative, and intensely focused, with the dark wooden desk surface blurred into a soft, shadowy backdrop.

Daniel appears strictly as a steady right hand framed by the ribbed cuff of his charcoal-grey crew-neck sweater. Holding a sharp drafting pencil, his fingers guide the graphite lead into the interior of an outlined streaming-multiprocessor rectangle. With deliberate strokes, he sketches a neat grid of smaller interior compartments representing execution cores, stacks of register files, and a dedicated rectangular tensor unit. He then draws fine, delicate arrows looping between the compartments to map internal data flow. Tiny particles of graphite dust accumulate along the fresh grey lines as the formerly empty block fills with intricate architectural detail. By the end of the shot, the single block has become a fully articulated compute schematic.

The camera maintains a low-angle macro close-up, executing a slow, steady slide across the paper to follow the pencil's movements. The depth of field is razor-thin, keeping the graphite tip, the freshly etched boxes, and paper fibers in crisp focus while softly defocusing the knit of his grey sleeve and the surrounding page.

annotation.beat: Macro on the paper as the pencil fills one multiprocessor block with smaller boxes for cores, registers and a tensor unit, then draws arrows of data flowing between them. Eraser crumbs and the lamp's warm light on the grain of the paper.

state.gpu_stage: detailed sketch of one compute block

shots.prompt:
Inside the home studio, a large cork board covers much of the wall above the workspace, densely patterned with colourful sticky notes, printed circuit schematics, and high-resolution silicon die photographs. Beside the board, an adjacent window reveals the first faint blue light of dawn seeping in from outside, creating a delicate natural contrast against the lingering warm tungsten glow of an off-screen desk lamp. The environment carries the quiet, solitary atmosphere of an all-night engineering session.

Seen from behind in a wide perspective, Daniel stands before the wall dressed in a charcoal-grey crew-neck sweater over a white T-shirt, dark jeans, and grey sneakers, his short dark-brown hair visible from the rear. He holds the newly completed paper bearing the detailed GPU multiprocessor architecture sketch, cleanly tears it free from the pad, and steps toward the wall. Raising his hands, he pushes a thumb tack through the top edge of the sheet, firmly pinning the architecture sketch directly into the vacant centre of the cork board among the surrounding reference materials.

The camera remains entirely stationary in a wide framing, letting the sprawling technical wall and the workspace dominate the composition while Daniel appears as a modest full-figure presence with his back turned. The framing emphasizes the physical progression of the design wall rather than a portrait, keeping the newly pinned sketch and the soft dawn light entering through the window clearly visible through the end of the shot.

annotation.beat: Daniel, seen from behind at medium-wide distance, tears out the page and pins it to the centre of a cork board covered with sticky notes and printed die photographs. Blue dawn light appears in the window beside the board.

state.gpu_stage: architecture sketch pinned on the cork board

shots.prompt:
A large wall-mounted whiteboard fills the frame in Daniel's home studio. Gentle, cool blue morning light filtering from a side window mixes with warm indoor overhead lighting, casting soft diagonal reflections across the glossy, clean melamine surface. Faint grey ghost marks and wiped dry-erase smudges from previous calculations are faintly visible around the margins, giving the space an authentic, work-in-progress atmosphere.

Daniel's face is out of frame; only his right hand and the wrist of his charcoal-grey crew-neck sweater are visible. He holds a black chisel-tip dry-erase marker with its cap posted securely on the back. Moving with practiced precision, the tip squeaks against the whiteboard, inking black logic symbols, parallel connection wires, and the internal NAND gates of a transistor-level full adder. He draws deliberate orthogonal trace lines connecting the input nodes through the gate array. Once the carry and sum paths are resolved, Daniel rotates the marker in his fingers and decisively taps the plastic cap against the final drawn output line. By the end of the shot, a neat, fully linked schematic for one adder circuit stands out in stark black lines on the white board.

The camera maintains an intimate close-up framing, tracking smoothly alongside the marker as it navigates the whiteboard surface. A shallow depth of field keeps the drawing tip and the freshly applied black ink in sharp focus while softly blurring the studio behind it. The frame remains locked strictly onto the hand, the marker, and the expanding circuit diagram.

annotation.beat: Close on a large whiteboard as a black marker in Daniel's hand draws a transistor-level circuit for one adder: NAND gates, a full adder and wires. The marker cap taps the output line.

state.gpu_stage: full-adder circuit on the whiteboard

shots.prompt:
The home studio is immersed in the quiet, focused ambience of late-night technical work. A large high-resolution monitor dominates the matte desk, casting a vivid cool illumination across the workspace that contrasts with the gentle amber glow of a distant desk lamp. The room is still and uncluttered, centering entirely on the crisp, luminescent display where intricate electronic design automation software operates in crisp detail.

The screen initially displays a heavily magnified view of a digital circuit layout: vibrant, sharp-edged rectangular ribbons and routing traces in saturated blues, reds, and cyans representing overlapping metal interconnect layers. In the foreground resting on the dark desk mat, Daniel’s right hand grips an ergonomic black mouse, his wrist framed by the ribbed cuff of a charcoal-grey crew-neck sweater. He clicks and rolls the mouse's central scroll wheel backward. In response, the virtual viewport smoothly zooms out. The isolated wire routings quickly recede into compact standard logic cells, which then assemble into repeating execution cores. By the end of the shot, the entire silicon floorplan sits visible as a massive, dense mosaic of identical glowing blocks framed by outer I/O rings, reflecting the architecture of a complete GPU die.

The camera begins in a tight macro close-up on the screen's glowing polygon lines, then executes a slow, deliberate zoom out to incorporate the monitor's thin black bezel and Daniel's hand on the mouse in the lower foreground. The focus remains locked onto the sharp visual architecture of the chip layout throughout, never tilting upward to reveal his face.

annotation.camera: close-up on the monitor, slow zoom out
annotation.beat: A monitor running chip layout software fills the frame: coloured rectangles of metal layers. The view zooms out until the whole die floorplan appears as a dense glowing mosaic of identical blocks, matching the paper sketch. Daniel's hand moves the mouse in the foreground.

state.gpu_stage: full die layout on the monitor

shots.prompt:
The interior entryway of the home studio is illuminated by soft, warm morning light, while the edges of the front door frame hint at a much brighter day outside. Pale neutral walls and clean, modern wood trim give the space an organized, calm atmosphere. A small console table stands near the threshold, and the overall color palette balances muted indoor earth tones with the crisp, cool illumination waiting just beyond the entryway.

Daniel is captured from behind in a waist-up view, displaying his short dark-brown hair and the back of his charcoal-grey crew-neck sweater, with a hint of a white T-shirt collar visible beneath it, paired with dark jeans. He smoothly slips into a durable blue denim jacket, pulling it on over the sweater and settling the shoulders. Reaching down, he picks up a tightly rolled large-format printout of the chip layout and slides it neatly inside a rigid black poster tube, securely pressing the cap into place. He slings the tube's black strap over his shoulder across his back, then reaches forward to turn the handle and open the front door into the brilliant morning daylight. By the end, he wears the denim jacket layered over his grey sweater with the poster tube safely slung over his shoulder, silhouetted against the bright exterior.

The camera remains static in a medium waist-height framing positioned directly behind him, keeping his hands, the denim jacket, and the black poster tube clearly visible throughout the action. The composition avoids any facial close-ups, prioritizing the deliberate physical preparation and the burst of daylight filling the open doorway.

annotation.beat: Morning. Seen from behind at waist height, Daniel pulls a denim jacket on over his grey sweater, slides a rolled layout printout into a black poster tube, slings it over his shoulder and opens the front door into bright daylight.

The exterior of a massive semiconductor fabrication facility stretches across the frame under a crisp, pale morning sky. Sunlight reflects sharply off the towering multi-story facade constructed of sheer glass panels, brushed steel beams, and clean white architectural accents. A sprawling, immaculately swept plaza paved with pale grey stone pavers extends in front of the structure, casting elongated, cool morning shadows. One hand loosely holds the nylon shoulder strap against his chest to steady the rolled layout printout inside as he advances across the expansive pavement.

The camera moves in a smooth, continuous wide tracking shot, gliding slowly forward and parallel to Daniel's path. The framing keeps him small in the lower third of the composition, deliberately dwarfed by the towering architecture of the fab rising above. shots.prompt:
The shot is set inside a brightly illuminated semiconductor fab gowning room. Cool fluorescent lighting floods the antiseptic white walls, glossy floor, and stainless steel benches, giving the space an immaculate, clinical atmosphere. Garment dispensers and sterile storage racks line the perimeter under sharp, shadowless light, establishing an environment engineered for strict contamination control.

Daniel stands beside a steel bench, initially appearing in his early thirties with short dark-brown hair, a neat beard, black rectangular glasses, and a denim jacket, resting a black poster tube on the bench. He steps into a pristine white cleanroom coverall, pulls it over his torso, and pulls the central zipper shut. He then draws the integrated white hood over his hair, loops a white face mask across his nose and mouth, and seats clear goggles over his glasses. Finally, he snaps bright blue nitrile gloves onto both hands, smoothing the cuffs. By the end, his everyday clothes are fully enclosed beneath the white bunny suit, hood, mask, goggles, and blue gloves, with nothing in his hands.

The camera maintains a static medium-wide framing throughout the shot, positioned at eye level across from the bench. The composition keeps Daniel visible from the mid-thighs up, documenting each step of the dressing sequence without zooming in or using facial close-ups. The sterile geometry of the gowning room remains fixed and steady as he prepares for the fab floor.

annotation.beat: In a bright white gowning room with steel benches, Daniel, at medium-wide distance, steps into a white cleanroom coverall, zips it, pulls on the white hood, a face mask, goggles over his glasses and blue nitrile gloves.

state.outfit: white cleanroom bunny suit, hood, face mask, goggles, blue gloves
state.gpu_stage: none in hand

shots.prompt:
The interior of the semiconductor fabrication facility's lithography bay is bathed in monochromatic amber-yellow safety lighting designed to protect photoresist-sensitive processes. Pristine polished metal panels and glossy off-white industrial surfaces softly reflect the warm golden hue, establishing an ultra-clean, sterile environment. In the immediate background, the exterior casing of an advanced photolithography scanner rises into the laminar airflow, its immaculate white chassis accented with dark status panels and precision access ports.

Two hands clad in blue nitrile gloves, extending from pristine white cleanroom suit sleeves, hold a transparent polycarbonate reticle pod. Inside the clear protective enclosure rests a square quartz photomask, a flawless plate of synthetic silica patterned with dark, opaque chrome. As the hands gently angle the carrier, the microscopic GPU circuit geometries etched into the chrome surface catch the amber light, glinting with fine, iridescent micro-architectural tracings. The gloved fingers carefully disengage the pod latch and align the quartz mask with the narrow reticle port of the scanner. With steady, deliberate motion, the hands slide the reticle into the motorized bay, where precision guide rails engage the edges and draw the mask smoothly into the scanner's enclosed optical column.

The camera maintains a crisp macro close-up, utilizing a shallow depth of field focused squarely on the intricate chrome patterns of the photomask. A slow, stable push-in tracks the movement as the glass plate travels from the carrier toward the machine interface. Daniel's face remains entirely off-screen, with only his blue-gloved fingers and white cuffs visible, keeping the visual emphasis wholly on the loaded component.

annotation.beat: In amber-yellow cleanroom light, gloved blue hands hold a clear pod containing a quartz photomask whose chrome pattern glitters with the GPU design, then slide it into the reticle port of a tall white lithography scanner.

state.outfit: blue nitrile gloves, white suit sleeves
state.gpu_stage: photomask of the design loaded into the scanner

shots.prompt:
Inside the semiconductor fab's lithography bay, dense amber-yellow photolithography-safe lighting casts a monochromatic glow across polished industrial panels and cleanroom equipment. Pristine white enamel housings and brushed stainless-steel surfaces surround the docking port, muted slightly by the strict wavelength-filtered illumination. Overhead, perforated laminar-flow ceiling filters trace subtle geometric patterns across reflective surfaces. The atmosphere is sterile, motionless, and strictly controlled.

A dark front-opening unified pod sits locked in position with its door retracted to reveal horizontal slots. A robotic end-effector made of matte grey anodized aluminum smoothly extends its slender vacuum wand beneath a pristine disc. The mechanical arm lifts a blank, mirror-polished 300-millimeter silicon wafer, completely free of any circuitry. Perfectly circular with a delicate edge bevel, the disc rises out of the carrier. As the robotic wrist slowly rotates, the flawless metallic surface catches and sweeps the amber cleanroom lamps and white ceiling panels across its mirror finish. No human operators are visible, keeping the focus entirely on the automated handling of the virgin substrate.

The camera maintains a close-up, object-focused insert on the wafer transfer, executing a steady, slow upward tilt that follows the disc's elevation. A shallow depth of field keeps the wafer’s razor-thin edge and pristine reflective plane sharply defined against the soft amber and charcoal machinery behind it. The tilt remains smooth and stable, tracking the reflective sweep until the silicon disc floats suspended in the center of the frame.

annotation.beat: A robotic arm lifts a blank, mirror-polished 300 millimetre silicon wafer out of a front-opening pod. The wafer reflects the amber lights and the white ceiling as it turns.

state.gpu_stage: blank mirror-polished silicon wafer

shots.prompt:
Inside the lithography bay of the cleanroom, the spin-coating chamber is viewed through a pristine transparent access window. Cool, clinical fab lighting merges with the warm yellow-amber safety illumination required for photo-sensitive processing, casting a rich golden glow across the polished stainless-steel interior. The cylindrical coater bowl is impeccably clean and isolated from airborne particles, creating a sterile, tightly controlled industrial atmosphere.

At the center of the chamber, a blank, mirror-polished three-hundred-millimetre silicon wafer rests securely atop a central vacuum chuck. A narrow automated dispense arm extends directly above the core and releases a single, viscous droplet of amber photoresist onto the pristine reflective disc. The chuck instantly accelerates into a high-speed spin. Centrifugal force flings the liquid outward in a rapid, seamless wave, evening it out into an ultra-thin layer. As the chemical coating stretches across the surface, optical interference generates vibrant, iridescent bands of magenta, violet, and green that ripple over the spinning surface, transforming the raw mirror disc into a finished photoresist-coated wafer.

The camera holds a locked-off close-up framed slightly from above, angled through the clear glass window directly onto the wafer's surface. Depth of field keeps the expanding liquid boundary and shimmering colour bands sharply defined while the outer metal housing softens in the background. The steady framing captures the full radial spread without panning, preserving the precise mechanical elegance of the automated coating cycle.

annotation.beat: Inside a coater a drop of photoresist lands on the wafer; the wafer spins fast and the liquid spreads into a thin film that flashes with iridescent colour bands.

state.gpu_stage: wafer coated with photoresist

shots.prompt:
The photolithography bay is bathed in monochromatic amber safe-lighting, casting a dense yellow glow across the immaculate cleanroom floor. A towering row of monolithic white scanner units stretches into the background, their polished composite panels reflecting overhead luminous ceiling grids. At the center of the line, a rhythmic, pulsing violet glow seeps faintly from the inspection seams and optical shielding of one active machine, hinting at the deep-ultraviolet laser exposure occurring within. The environment feels hermetic, sterile, and dominated by massive high-precision industrial tooling.

Daniel appears as a small, full-bodied figure dwarfed beside the scanner, dressed head-to-toe in a cleanroom bunny suit. The white hooded coverall, zip-up booties, nitrile gloves, and face mask fully conceal his usual clothing, leaving only his dark-rimmed glasses visible beneath protective clear eyewear. Standing before the machine's extended terminal arm, he operates the dual control monitors, inputting alignment parameters and verifying that the photoresist-coated wafer is properly exposing beneath the reticle. He remains stationed at the console throughout, monitoring diagnostic readouts as the violet light pulses steadily beside him.

The camera frames the expanse in a wide perspective, performing a slow, cinematic dolly across the polished bay floor. The composition emphasizes the sheer physical scale of the scanner architecture, keeping the environment dominant while Daniel stands as an understated, full-figure silhouette in the middle ground. The ambient amber lighting and rhythmic violet pulse remain constant throughout the smooth tracking movement, preserving an authentic documentary feel.

annotation.beat: Wide view of the amber photolithography bay: a row of tall white scanners. A pulsing violet glow leaks from one machine. Daniel, a small white-suited figure, stands at its control monitors.

state.gpu_stage: wafer being exposed

shots.prompt:
The photolithography bay's ambient amber safety lighting casts a warm monochromatic wash across the control console, contrasting against the crisp, cool luminescence radiating from the scanner's display screen. The cleanroom atmosphere is sterile, silent, and technologically precise, marked by the absolute absence of airborne dust and the faint reflections glancing across the anti-glare glass of the terminal monitor.

The industrial LCD monitor displays a dark diagnostic interface tracking the active lithography cycle. Centered on the interface, a detailed digital circular wafer map shows a dense grid of rectangular chip fields. Field by field, pale translucent blocks turn into solid bright green squares as the stepper pulses UV light onto each respective die location. Beneath the filling circle, a slender horizontal progress bar and percentage readout tick upward in real time. Daniel’s right hand, clad in a fitted blue nitrile cleanroom glove emerging from the gathered cuff of a clean white bunny suit sleeve, reaches into frame. His gloved index finger points deliberately at the advancing progress bar, holding steady alongside the readout as three more rectangular exposure dies sequentially illuminate across the wafer grid.

The camera holds a locked-off, slightly angled close-up insert on the monitor face and the gesturing hand. A shallow depth of field keeps the glowing die matrix and the textured blue fingertip in sharp clarity, while blurring the surrounding console bezel and the amber-tinted machinery behind it into a soft, steady backdrop.

annotation.beat: On the scanner monitor a circular wafer map fills in field by field with exposed rectangles, while a gloved blue finger points at the progress bar.

state.gpu_stage: wafer exposure progress map filling

shots.prompt:
The cleanroom etch bay maintains a subdued, sterile atmosphere, where cool overhead ambient lighting recedes against heavy industrial machinery. The stainless-steel vacuum chamber dominates the space, its brushed metallic surfaces catching faint clinical highlights. Deep within the chamber's sealed interior, an intense luminance takes over as process gases ignite. An ethereal magenta and electric-purple glow illuminates the dark cavity, casting shifting violet hues and dancing specular highlights across the surrounding bolted flanges and polished steel framework.

Through the thick, circular quartz viewport set into the heavy vacuum flange, the interior of the etch chamber is sharply detailed. The circular silicon wafer rests flat upon a dark ceramic electrostatic chuck, its mirrored surface crisscrossed with microscopic circuit geometries. A vibrant cloud of magenta-purple plasma burns steadily suspended just millimeters above the wafer. The luminous gas flickers with subtle, high-frequency turbulence, bombarding the exposed silicon with reactive ions to carve the GPU's intricate patterns into the dies. No person is visible in frame, leaving the automated microfabrication reaction to unfold in absolute isolation as the glowing violet light ripples across the reflective disc.

The camera remains locked in a tight macro insert framing the round glass viewport. The circular window and its heavy hex bolts anchor the composition, maintaining crisp focus on the wafer surface and the incandescent plasma hovering above it. The camera holds steady, capturing the subtle flutter of purple light as it casts iridescent reflections against the beveled glass and steel rim.

annotation.beat: Through the round viewport of a vacuum etch chamber, a magenta-purple plasma glows above the wafer as the pattern is etched in, the light flickering on the steel frame.

state.gpu_stage: wafer in the etch chamber

shots.prompt:
Inside the semiconductor cleanroom etch bay, cool, sterile fluorescent lighting floods the industrial space, casting soft, diffuse reflections against stainless steel vacuum equipment and filtered ventilation panels in the blurred backdrop. The environment feels immaculately controlled, silent, and clinical, illuminated by balanced neutral-white work lights that prevent harsh glare across the delicate machinery.

Two hands encased in snug, powder-free blue nitrile gloves securely grasp the ergonomic edges of a specialized black wafer-handling frame. Centered inside sits a three-hundred-millimeter circular silicon disc, transformed by the etching process into a dense, flawless grid containing hundreds of identical rectangular GPU dies separated by fine scribe lines. The gloved fingers steadily tilt the disc a few degrees backward and forward under the overhead illumination. As the flat plane angles against the light sources, microscopic etched pathways act as a diffraction grating, sweeping vivid iridescent waves of violet, emerald green, cyan, and shimmering gold across the repetitive array of microchips.

The camera frames the disc in a sharp, object-focused close-up, executing a slow, graceful orbit around the edge of the wafer holder. The shallow depth of field isolates the glittering geometric surface against the out-of-focus glove tips and distant machine housings, keeping the dynamic prismatic reflections and razor-sharp die borders consistently centered and crisp throughout the smooth floating movement.

annotation.beat: Gloved blue hands hold up the finished wafer in a wafer holder. Its surface is now a precise grid of hundreds of identical rectangular dies that split the light into rainbow colours as it tilts.

state.gpu_stage: patterned wafer with a rainbow grid of dies

shots.prompt:
The automated testing bay of the fabrication facility is bathed in cool, clinical LED light, supplemented by an intense circular illuminator focused directly onto the probe workstation. Precision-machined steel surfaces, matte black vacuum stages, and sterile machine enclosures define the immediate surroundings, while the patterned silicon wafer below glints with faint prism highlights. The atmosphere is quiet, sterile, and technologically exacting, capturing a stage of rigorous automated verification.

The patterned silicon wafer rests securely atop a circular, dark-grey vacuum chuck. Positioned directly above it, a specialized probe card features dozens of hair-thin, angled metallic needles clustered in a tight geometric array matching the die's contact pads. No human hands or clothing enter the frame during the automated sequence. The chuck indexes beneath the probe head with rigid, microscopic lateral steps. Each time the stage pauses, the cluster of needle tips descends smoothly to touch the microscopic pads of a single rectangular die. A tiny, pinpoint contact flash of bright white-gold light glints at the needle junctions as test current pulses through the integrated circuitry, before the needles retract fractionally and the chuck shifts to align the adjacent die on the wafer grid.

The camera holds an extreme macro close-up at a shallow, low-angled perspective, maintaining a razor-thin depth of field locked onto the needle array and the die surface beneath. The surrounding machinery blurs softly into the background, keeping the entire focus on the rhythmic stepping motion, the electrical flashes, and the iridescent micro-etched silicon throughout the shot.

annotation.beat: Macro of a probe card: dozens of fine needles touch down on one die after another on the wafer resting on a probe-station chuck, a tiny contact flash each time.

state.gpu_stage: patterned wafer under probe test

shots.prompt:
The fab test floor maintains a cool, sterile ambiance dominated by dark workstation consoles and the hum of precision electronics. Overhead cleanroom fixtures cast soft, neutral white light across the matte plastic bezel of an industrial diagnostics monitor, while the surrounding testing floor falls off into muted grey shadows. The glowing display serves as the primary light source, washing the immediate foreground in a faint digital luminescence.

The flat screen presents a crisp interface centered on a full circular wafer map partitioned into hundreds of square die segments. Across the circular grid, the individual dies register their probe results, steadily populating the interior with solid, bright green passing indicators, leaving only a tiny scatter of red failure markers around the extreme outer edge. A hand clad in a sterile powder-free blue nitrile glove enters from the lower right of the frame, pausing directly before the glowing map. Daniel gives a firm, steady thumbs-up gesture against the screen's emerald glow, celebrating the outstanding production yield on the freshly probed wafer.

The camera holds a steady close-up on the workstation monitor, framing the digital wafer yield graph squarely in the middle of the composition. The razor-sharp die boundaries remain pin-sharp throughout the shot, with the blurred edges of fab machinery lingering in the soft background. The gloved hand stays partially silhouetted against the bright display, emphasizing the successful milestone before the shot concludes.

annotation.beat: A monitor shows a circular wafer map filling with mostly green squares and a few red ones at the edge. A gloved blue hand gives a thumbs-up in front of the screen.

state.gpu_stage: tested wafer with a mostly green yield map

shots.prompt:
The shot takes place inside the enclosed work chamber of an automated wafer dicing station within the cleanroom fab. Crisp, neutral-white LED illumination reflects off wet brushed-steel fixtures, drainage channels, and clear polycarbonate splash shields. A fine aerosolized mist hangs in the air, catching the cool industrial light and coating the surrounding metal surfaces with tiny, glistening condensation droplets. The atmosphere is sterile, clinical, and intensely mechanical.

Secured on a vacuum chuck below, the circular silicon wafer rests flat against adhesive blue dicing tape stretched tight inside a circular metal ring frame. The wafer's mirror-smooth surface displays an intricate grid of identical iridescent GPU dies, shimmering with faint amber and turquoise interference tones. Above it, an ultra-thin diamond-grit saw blade spins at tens of thousands of revolutions per minute, blurrily transparent from sheer velocity. A dual nozzle directs a continuous, pressurized stream of deionized water right onto the contact point. The spinning blade glides steadily along a narrow street between the microscopic circuits, slicing cleanly through the brittle crystalline silicon to cut precise straight channels while leaving the underlying blue tape intact. Fine liquid spray shears outward across the wafer as the continuous grid divides into separate, freestanding square dies.

The camera holds a macro close-up framing, positioned at a low angle that emphasizes the razor-thin profile of the spinning blade against the silicon plane. The depth of field remains exceptionally shallow, maintaining tack-sharp focus on the cutting contact zone and the dancing water droplets while the edges of the wafer softly blur. A smooth, subtle horizontal tracking motion follows just behind the advancing blade, keeping the glistening saw kerf and the newly separated silicon edges continuously in view.

annotation.beat: A thin diamond saw blade spins and cuts straight lines through the wafer under a fine spray of water, separating the grid into individual dies.

state.gpu_stage: wafer being diced into dies

shots.prompt:
